text.title: Fitness-Function Suite Bootstrap — Worked Example
text.summary: One complete five-function starter suite for an orders API (k6 p95 nightly, pipeline duration from CI, import-linter layers, lizard complexity ratchet with a baseline file, oasdiff breaking-change gate) with the four weekly reviews filled in and a note on each non-obvious value; then a three-function launch that the validator rejects and why.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: orders-api, a Python service with a `http` / `application` / `domain` / `infrastructure` layout, a published OpenAPI v1.12.0, and a GitHub Actions pipeline. The team agreed on evolutionary architecture a quarter ago and has shipped nothing. The architect (arch:alice) bootstraps five functions, launches all of them non-blocking on 2026-09-07, and promotes the layer guard at the second weekly review.

example.title: ffsb-orders-api

example.note: Five functions, one per category; three extra slots are left empty on purpose (r-ffsb-five-to-eight-functions). `checkout-p95` runs nightly on a dedicated runner with the load profile committed at `perf/profiles/checkout-v2.json`, so a red means the service got slower, not that a neighbour job compiled (r-ffsb-perf-p95-under-fixed-load). `pipeline-duration` is computed by `ci/pipeline_duration.py` from the last 20 runs and its unit is minutes (r-ffsb-deploy-lead-time-from-ci). `layer-direction` is the only blocking function and carries a promotion record: nine green runs on main, approved by arch:alice at the 2026-09-21 review (r-ffsb-ratchet-first-then-block). `cyclomatic-complexity` has 173 current violators in `quality/complexity-baseline.txt` and fails only on new ones, so its threshold is 0 new violations, not 0 violations (r-ffsb-complexity-ratchet-with-baseline). `openapi-breaking-diff` names the released schema it diffs against (r-ffsb-contract-breaking-change-gate). The first review recorded `checkout-p95` red and the action taken; the fourth set the ongoing cadence (r-ffsb-owner-and-weekly-review).

example.title: three blocking functions on day one
example.note: What the validator prints: `functions` has 3 items, fewer than minItems 5, and no element has category deployability or contract (r-ffsb-five-to-eight-functions); `checkout-p95` has `runs_on: pull_request`, not post_merge or nightly (r-ffsb-perf-p95-under-fixed-load); all three are `mode: blocking` with no `promotion` record (r-ffsb-ratchet-first-then-block); `cyclomatic-complexity` has no `baseline_file` while its baseline is 173 violators against a threshold of 0 (r-ffsb-complexity-ratchet-with-baseline). What the reviewer sees: a complexity job red on its first run, a latency job that fails whenever the runner is busy, and a team that adds `continue-on-error: true` by Friday (fm-blocking-on-day-one, fm-perf-on-shared-runner).
